text.p: Following are some of the historical events which took place on October 31.
1517 - Martin Luther posted his 95 theses, an attack on various ecclesiastical abuses, on the door of Wittenberg Palace, marking the beginning of the Protestant Reformation in Germany.
1632 - Jan Vermeer, one of the masters of Dutch art in the 17th century, born.
1705 - Pope Clement XIV born as Giovanni Vincenzo Antonio Ganganelli. He was made a cardinal in 1759 and became Pope in 1769.
1795 - English poet John Keats, best known for such odes as "On a Grecian Urn" and "To a Nightingale" born.
1838 - King Luis I of Portugal born. His reign from 1861 to 1889 was noted for its political and economic reforms.
1864 - Nevada was admitted to the union as the 36th state of the United States.
1887 - Chiang Kai-Shek, who ruled China from 1928 to 1949, born. His Nationalist government was driven from the mainland by the Communists and formed a government-in-exile on Taiwan.
1888 - John Boyd Dunlop took out a patent for his pneumatic bicycle tyre.
1922 - Prince Norodom Sihanouk of Cambodia born.
1926 - Harry Houdini, magician famed for his escape acts, died. Born Ehrich Weiss, he named himself after the French magician Robert-Houdin.
1940 - The Battle of Britain, the struggle between Germany and Britain over air control of the English Channel, was officially designated to have ended on October 31.
1956 - Britain and Frrance bombed Egyptian airfields during the Suez crisis.
1961 - Russia's de-Stalinisation programme reached a climax when his body was removed from the mausoleum in Red Square and re-buried.
1968 - President Lyndon Johnson ordered a complete cessation of American bombing of North Vietnam.
1968 - Mexican actor Ramon Navarro died.
1974 - Britain, France and the U.S. vetoed a motion at the U.N. to expel South Africa.
1979 - A DC-10 crashed after landing on the wrong runway at Mexico City's airport; 75 people were killed.
1984 - Indian Prime Minister Indira Gandhi was assassinated by three Sikh members of her bodyguard.
1994 - An American Eagle commuter flight en route from Indianapolis to Chicago crashed in a corn field during a windy rainstorm, killing all 68 on board.
1994 - British art historian Sir John Pope-Hennessy, one of the world's leading authorities on Italian Renaissance work, died.
1995 - A Nigerian military-appointed court sentenced Ogoni minority rights leader Ken Saro-Wiwa and three others to death for murder.
